summary_paragraph: A woman with a history of type 1 diabetes and anxiety was readmitted for abdominal pain, vomiting, and diabetic ketoacidosis with an anion gap of 28. She had been recently discharged but re-presented with recurrent symptoms and hyperglycemia. She was treated in the MICU with an insulin drip, which was transitioned to subcutaneous insulin as her metabolic panel stabilized. The abdominal pain lacked an organic cause—lipase was normal, imaging from a prior admission showed only chronic colonic wall thickening, and a gastric emptying study was normal, ruling out gastroparesis. STI testing and urine analysis showed no active infection requiring treatment, though Gardnerella was noted for outpatient follow-up. Her acute kidney injury resolved with hydration. Tachycardia improved but persisted mildly, likely due to anxiety and volume status. Psychiatric factors were considered significant contributors to her symptom burden, and she was discharged on scheduled as-needed lorazepam. She was instructed to adhere strictly to insulin therapy and follow up with primary care, GI, and psychiatry.
